title: How Does Cut Grass Grow Back? Explained Simply | PUC Biology Class 11
description:
The college lawn was cut short on Monday, and by Friday the grass was tall again, even though its tips were cut off. Diya asks: if the tips are gone, where is the grass growing from? The answer is a special tissue whose cells keep dividing.

This topic is not in the current NCERT text but is in the ISC syllabus. You will see what a tissue is, then a zoom ladder from a plant to the shoot tip, the root tip and the meristem cells themselves (thin walls, dense cytoplasm, a large nucleus). A meristem cell grows, divides, piles up behind the tip and leaves behind cells that become permanent. Then the three kinds of meristem, apical, intercalary and lateral, plus the axillary bud, primary vs secondary meristems side by side, a pause and think about grazing, six meristems sorted, the intercalary exam trap, an original assertion and reason question with a full solution, a recap card and three questions. This is Episode 49 of our PUC Biology series.

Made for NCERT, CBSE, ISC (CISCE), PUC (Karnataka) and NEET students.
